what.text: Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, also called choline alfoscerate) is a choline-containing compound described in research as a precursor of acetylcholine, a nerve messenger.

src.label: De Jesus Moreno Moreno, Clin Ther, PubMed
Jeon et al., BMC Geriatrics, PubMed

what.text: In the US it is sold in dietary supplements; the NIH label database lists hundreds of supplement labels matching 'alpha-GPC'. In Italy it is an authorised medicine (Gliatilin, Delecit).

what.text: This page covers alpha-GPC taken by mouth. The site's separate Choline page covers choline chloride, the form used in injections.

research.text: Most human trials of alpha-GPC are in older adults with dementia or mild memory problems, several from Italy and South Korea. Studies of energy, focus or strength in healthy people are small and short. A large Korean health-records study linked its use to more strokes. Each study is listed as it was run.

research.title: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (Clin Ther 2003)

facts.v: De Jesus Moreno Moreno M. Clin Ther 2003;25(1):178-93
multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
261 people aged 60 to 80 with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (199 women, 62 men)
choline alfoscerate 400 mg capsules or placebo, 3 times a day
180 days
ADAS-Cog, MMSE and other dementia scales

research.found: ADAS-Cog scores improved by 3.20 points on choline alfoscerate and worsened by 2.90 points on placebo by day 180. The other scales also differed between groups. The author reported it was well tolerated.

src.label: De Jesus Moreno Moreno, Clin Ther, PubMed

research.title: Mild cognitive impairment (BMC Geriatr 2024)

facts.v: Jeon J, Lee SY, Lee S, et al. BMC Geriatr 2024;24(1):774
multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (KCT0008797)
100 people with mild cognitive impairment
600 mg alpha-GPC soft capsule or placebo
12 weeks
ADAS-Cog; side effects and lab tests

research.found: ADAS-Cog improved by 2.34 points, significantly more than on placebo. No serious side effects were reported, and side-effect rates did not differ between groups.

src.label: Jeon et al., BMC Geriatrics, PubMed

research.title: Single dose, thinking tests in trained men (Nutrients 2024)

facts.v: Kerksick CM. Nutrients 2024;16(23):4240
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover
20 resistance-trained men, mean age 31
a single dose of 630 mg or 315 mg alpha-GPC, or placebo
single sessions
Stroop, N-Back and Flanker tests; mood scales; jump and bench-press power; growth hormone

research.found: Stroop scores rose more after both doses than after placebo. N-Back and Flanker results, mood ratings, physical performance and growth hormone did not differ.

src.label: Kerksick, Nutrients, PubMed

research.title: Six days and muscle force (J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2015)

facts.v: Bellar D, LeBlanc NR, Campbell B. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2015;12:42
double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with a 1-week washout
13 college-aged men
600 mg alpha-GPC a day or placebo
6 days per period
isometric mid-thigh pull and upper-body force

research.found: Peak lower-body force rose more on alpha-GPC (+98.8 N vs -39.0 N on placebo; P=0.044). The upper-body change was not significant.

src.label: Bellar et al., J Int Soc Sports Nutr, PubMed

research.title: Alpha-GPC use and stroke over 10 years (JAMA Netw Open 2021)

facts.v: Lee G, Choi S, Chang J, et al. JAMA Netw Open 2021;4(11):e2136008
retrospective cohort using national health insurance data; not a trial
12,008,977 adults aged 50 or older without stroke or Alzheimer's; 108,877 were prescribed alpha-GPC in 2006-2008
follow-up from 2009 to January 2018
total, ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke

research.found: After matching, users had a higher risk of total stroke (adjusted hazard ratio 1.43), ischemic stroke (1.34) and hemorrhagic stroke (1.37), rising with longer use. This shows an association, not cause. A correction to the methods was published in 2026.

us.text: Alpha-GPC is not an FDA-approved drug. In the US it is sold as a dietary supplement, which FDA does not review for safety or effectiveness before sale. As of November 1, 2026.

side.text: FDA does not review dietary supplements for safety before sale. The trials above reported few side effects. A large Korean health-records study linked alpha-GPC use to a higher stroke risk.

items.text: in the 2024 Korean trial of 100 people, no serious side effects were reported and side-effect rates matched placebo. The 2003 Alzheimer's trial author reported it was well tolerated.

items.text: people prescribed alpha-GPC had about 43% higher adjusted stroke risk over 10 years than matched non-users, with a dose-response pattern. The authors noted that choline has been linked to heart disease through TMAO, a product of gut bacteria, and said the mechanism needs study. The study cannot show cause.
